FINAL IVX REGISTRATION + MEMBER AUTHENTICATION CLOSEOUT
SIGN UP, SIGN IN, PASSWORD RECOVERY, SESSION, MEMBER CREATION — END TO END

EXECUTE NOW.
DO NOT RETURN ANOTHER GENERAL ENTERPRISE REPORT.
DO NOT ADD UNRELATED FEATURES.
DO NOT MARK COMPLETE FROM SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY.

The objective is to make registration and authentication reliable for:

- Owner
- Admin
- Member
- Investor
- Buyer
- Realtor
- Staff

Platforms:

- Public landing page
- Android app
- iPhone/iOS
- Web portal
- IVX IA Chat login where applicable

==================================================
CURRENT KNOWN STATUS
==================================================

Already implemented or partially proven:

- Registration orchestrator
- Registration state machine
- Request ID and trace ID
- Duplicate-submit protection
- Error normalization
- Live backend canary
- Registration metrics
- Auth and member creation flow
- Password redaction
- Backend tests

Known remaining risks:

- Custom SMTP not configured
- Registration database migration not applied
- CloudFront may serve stale index.html
- Physical-device/browser QA incomplete
- Full email-confirmation and password-reset proof incomplete
- Sign-in must be tested after registration
- Owner and ordinary-member flows must remain separate
- Partial-account recovery must be proven
- Real production data must not be duplicated or lost

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE AND CAPTURE BASELINE
==================================================

Before editing:

1. Record current GitHub HEAD.
2. Record current Render runtime SHA.
3. Record current landing-page asset checksums.
4. Record current APK version and version code.
5. Capture current auth configuration without exposing keys.
6. Capture current registration database constraints.
7. Record active Supabase project reference.
8. Record CloudFront ETag and cache age.
9. Record current registration metrics.
10. Capture one failed and one successful test attempt with trace IDs.

Return:

BASELINE_GITHUB_SHA:
BASELINE_RUNTIME_SHA:
SUPABASE_PROJECT:
LANDING_INDEX_ETAG:
APK_VERSION:
REGISTRATION_HEALTH:
OPEN_BLOCKERS:

==================================================
PHASE 2 — ONE CANONICAL AUTH ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Create or verify one shared authentication layer.

Required:

- one canonical Supabase URL;
- one canonical anon/publishable key;
- one server-only service-role key;
- one shared auth client factory;
- one shared session manager;
- one shared error mapper;
- one shared role/authorization verifier.

All modules must use the same configuration:

- landing registration;
- landing login;
- member portal;
- owner login;
- Android;
- iOS;
- web;
- password recovery;
- session restore.

Reject:

- duplicate Supabase clients;
- staging URLs in production;
- old environment names;
- Rork URLs;
- hardcoded passwords;
- local password comparisons;
- fake owner sessions;
- manual JWT creation in the client.

Required proof:

AUTH_CONFIG_SINGLE_SOURCE: PASS / FAIL
ALL_CLIENTS_USE_PRODUCTION_PROJECT: PASS / FAIL
SERVICE_ROLE_IN_CLIENT_BUNDLE: YES / NO
DUPLICATE_AUTH_CLIENTS: COUNT

==================================================
PHASE 3 — PRODUCTION DATABASE CONSTRAINTS
==================================================

Execute the committed registration migration in production.

Required unique constraints:

- profiles.auth_user_id UNIQUE
- members.auth_user_id UNIQUE
- members.normalized_email UNIQUE where architecture requires it
- landing_investments.registration_request_id UNIQUE
- registration_requests.request_id UNIQUE

Required foreign keys:

- profiles.auth_user_id → auth.users.id
- members.auth_user_id → auth.users.id
- landing_investments.member_id → members.id
- landing_investments.opportunity_id → deals.id

Required checks:

- no duplicate current rows;
- safe cleanup plan for pre-existing duplicates;
- migration is idempotent;
- rollback SQL is documented;
- RLS remains enabled;
- users cannot assign owner/admin roles to themselves.

Do not disable RLS globally.

Return:

MIGRATION_FILE:
MIGRATION_EXECUTED:
PRODUCTION_RESULT:
INDEXES_CREATED:
FOREIGN_KEYS_CREATED:
DUPLICATES_FOUND:
DUPLICATES_REPAIRED:
ROLLBACK_PLAN:

==================================================
PHASE 4 — CUSTOM SMTP AND EMAIL DELIVERY
==================================================

Configure owner-controlled production SMTP.

Required:

- sender domain;
- sender name;
- sender address;
- SMTP host;
- SMTP port;
- secure transport;
- SPF;
- DKIM;
- DMARC;
- Supabase Auth SMTP settings;
- allowed redirect URLs;
- landing callback URL;
- Android deep link;
- iOS universal link;
- web recovery route.

Verify live delivery for:

1. New-account confirmation.
2. Password reset.
3. Resend confirmation.
4. Email-change confirmation if supported.
5. Owner security notification if implemented.

Never display SMTP credentials.

Return:

SMTP_CONFIGURED:
SPF:
DKIM:
DMARC:
CONFIRMATION_EMAIL_DELIVERED:
RESET_EMAIL_DELIVERED:
RESEND_EMAIL_DELIVERED:
DELIVERY_TIME:
FAILED_EMAIL_TRACE_ID:

If owner SMTP values are genuinely unavailable, mark only this phase BLOCKED and list the exact owner action. Do not ask for credentials unless the configured values have been checked and proven missing.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — PUBLIC MEMBER SIGN-UP
==================================================

Test the live landing page with a new disposable email.

Required flow:

Step 1:
- Select opportunity.
- Enter amount or interest level.
- Preserve deal context.

Step 2:
- Enter permitted investor-interest information.
- Preserve form state.

Step 3:
- First name.
- Last name.
- Email.
- Password.
- Create Account & Continue.

Backend flow:

FORM
→ VALIDATION
→ REQUEST ID
→ AUTH USER
→ MEMBER/PROFILE
→ INVESTMENT INTEREST
→ SESSION OR EMAIL CONFIRMATION
→ STEP 4

Required:

- button disables on submit;
- one logical request per tap;
- password never logged;
- duplicate email maps to Login/Reset;
- weak password maps correctly;
- invalid email maps correctly;
- service errors show trace ID;
- entered non-sensitive fields remain after recoverable failure;
- no duplicate Auth user;
- no duplicate member;
- no duplicate interest row;
- selected deal and amount remain.

Return:

SIGNUP_REQUEST_ID:
TRACE_ID:
AUTH_USER_CREATED:
MEMBER_CREATED:
PROFILE_CREATED:
INTEREST_CREATED:
SESSION_CREATED:
EMAIL_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED:
STEP_4_OPENED:
DUPLICATE_COUNTS:

==================================================
PHASE 6 — MEMBER SIGN-IN
==================================================

Test the member created in Phase 5.

Required:

1. Correct email/password login.
2. Wrong password rejection.
3. Wrong email rejection.
4. Email case normalization.
5. Password symbols preserved.
6. Double-tap prevention.
7. Session saved.
8. Member profile loads.
9. Correct member role loads.
10. Member is blocked from owner/admin routes.
11. Selected opportunity context is restored where applicable.
12. No full-page crash.
13. No infinite spinner.
14. Clear error message with trace ID.

Return:

CORRECT_LOGIN:
WRONG_PASSWORD:
WRONG_EMAIL:
ROLE:
MEMBER_ROUTE:
OWNER_ROUTE_REJECTED:
SESSION_ID_REDACTED:
TRACE_IDS:

==================================================
PHASE 7 — OWNER SIGN-IN
==================================================

Test the canonical owner separately.

Do not change owner password unless reset is required.

Verify:

- production Supabase project;
- canonical owner user exists;
- email confirmed;
- account not banned;
- password sign-in;
- owner role verified server-side;
- Owner Dashboard;
- Admin Hub;
- Variables;
- Settings;
- IVX IA Chat;
- logout;
- login again;
- app restart persistence;
- invalid password rejection;
- non-owner rejection.

MFA:

- optional;
- default OFF;
- managed under Settings → Security;
- normal login must work without MFA.

Return:

OWNER_AUTH:
OWNER_ROLE:
OWNER_DASHBOARD:
ADMIN_HUB:
VARIABLES:
LOGOUT_LOGIN:
RESTART_PERSISTENCE:
INVALID_PASSWORD:
NON_OWNER_REJECTION:
MFA_DEFAULT:

==================================================
PHASE 8 — PASSWORD RECOVERY
==================================================

Test for owner and ordinary member.

Required flow:

Forgot Password
→ reset email
→ approved callback/deep link
→ recovery session
→ new password
→ old password rejected
→ new password accepted
→ session policy applied

Test:

- valid link;
- expired link;
- reused link;
- resend;
- wrong email;
- rate limit;
- browser refresh during recovery;
- Android deep link;
- iOS/web callback when available.

Do not put passwords in URLs, logs, analytics, or evidence.

Return:

OWNER_RESET:
MEMBER_RESET:
EMAIL_DELIVERY:
DEEP_LINK:
OLD_PASSWORD_REJECTED:
NEW_PASSWORD_ACCEPTED:
EXPIRED_LINK:
REUSED_LINK:
RESET_TRACE_IDS:

==================================================
PHASE 9 — SESSION MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Verify:

- access token refresh;
- refresh-token rotation;
- secure session persistence;
- app restart;
- browser refresh;
- background/foreground;
- network loss;
- reconnect;
- logout;
- logout all devices if available;
- password change invalidates old session;
- disabled user is rejected;
- no refresh loop;
- no fake fallback session.

Do not store plaintext passwords.

Return:

SESSION_RESTORE:
TOKEN_REFRESH:
BACKGROUND_FOREGROUND:
NETWORK_RECOVERY:
LOGOUT:
LOGOUT_ALL:
PASSWORD_CHANGE_INVALIDATION:
STORAGE_AUDIT:

==================================================
PHASE 10 — PARTIAL-ACCOUNT REPAIR
==================================================

Test and repair:

CASE A:
Auth user exists, member missing.

CASE B:
Member exists, interest missing.

CASE C:
Registration request completed but client timed out.

CASE D:
Duplicate submission arrives after completion.

CASE E:
Email confirmation completed after browser closed.

Required:

- resume using request ID;
- create only missing record;
- never create duplicate identity;
- preserve deal/amount;
- return final canonical result.

Return:

CASE_A:
CASE_B:
CASE_C:
CASE_D:
CASE_E:
DUPLICATES_CREATED:
REPAIR_LOG:

==================================================
PHASE 11 — ROLE AND AUTHORIZATION QA
==================================================

Test real server authorization for:

- owner;
- admin;
- member;
- investor;
- buyer;
- realtor;
- staff;
- suspended user;
- unauthenticated user.

Verify:

- role is not accepted from untrusted client input;
- owner/admin cannot be self-assigned;
- user sees only permitted records;
- RLS blocks cross-user access;
- backend verifies JWT;
- service-role key stays server-side;
- protected APIs return 401/403 correctly.

Return a matrix:

ROLE:
LOGIN:
ALLOWED_ROUTES:
DENIED_ROUTES:
API_RESULT:
RLS_RESULT:

==================================================
PHASE 12 — ERROR AND RETRY BEHAVIOR
==================================================

Test:

- 400 validation error;
- 401 authentication;
- 403 authorization;
- 409 duplicate;
- 429 rate limit;
- 500 server failure;
- 502/503/504 temporary failure;
- request timeout;
- malformed JSON;
- stale frontend bundle;
- missing config;
- Supabase unavailable.

Rules:

- automatic retry only for safe temporary failures;
- maximum 3 attempts;
- exponential backoff;
- query request status before retry after timeout;
- invalid credentials never auto-retry;
- duplicates return existing result;
- no crash;
- no lost form context.

Return:

ERROR_CODE:
USER_MESSAGE:
RETRYABLE:
ATTEMPTS:
TRACE_ID:
FINAL_STATE:

==================================================
PHASE 13 — CLOUDFRONT AND ASSET PARITY
==================================================

Invalidate:

- /index.html
- registration JavaScript assets
- portal JavaScript assets
- auth configuration asset if separate

Verify:

- no stale index;
- correct Content-Length;
- ETag;
- Last-Modified;
- SHA-256;
- current GitHub commit marker;
- current configuration marker;
- mobile and desktop receive the same current build.

Return:

DISTRIBUTION_ID:
INVALIDATION_ID:
STATUS:
INDEX_ETAG:
INDEX_SHA256:
INVEST_JS_SHA256:
PORTAL_JS_SHA256:
CACHE_STATUS:
ASSET_COMMIT:

==================================================
PHASE 14 — PHYSICAL-DEVICE AND BROWSER QA
==================================================

Run the complete flow on:

- Samsung Browser;
- Android Chrome;
- desktop Chrome;
- iPhone Safari;
- desktop Safari where available.

Test matrix:

1. New signup.
2. Existing email.
3. Correct login.
4. Wrong password.
5. Forgot password.
6. Email confirmation.
7. Session persistence.
8. Refresh.
9. Back button.
10. Autofill.
11. Password manager.
12. Keyboard.
13. Orientation.
14. Slow 4G.
15. Network loss.
16. Reconnect.
17. Duplicate tap.
18. Browser background/return.
19. Step 4 continuation.
20. Logout/login.

Owner-controlled physical testing may be required where the execution environment has no real device. In that case, produce a QR/link-based guided test and record owner-confirmed results with timestamps. Do not falsely mark device QA as executed inside a sandbox.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — REGISTRATION AND AUTH METRICS
==================================================

Owner dashboard must show:

- signups started;
- signups completed;
- signups failed;
- completion rate;
- abandonment rate;
- failure by stage;
- failure by error code;
- duplicate attempts;
- rate-limited attempts;
- average completion time;
- confirmation completion;
- login success;
- login failure;
- password reset requested;
- password reset completed;
- session refresh failure.

No sensitive values in metrics.

Verify dashboard values against API/database records.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — AUTOMATED TEST SUITE
==================================================

Required automated tests:

1. Valid member signup.
2. Duplicate signup.
3. Weak password.
4. Invalid email.
5. Missing config.
6. Auth succeeds/profile fails.
7. Profile succeeds/interest fails.
8. Retry resumes.
9. Duplicate tap creates one account.
10. Timeout after Auth.
11. Correct member login.
12. Wrong password.
13. Owner login.
14. Non-owner owner-route rejection.
15. Password reset.
16. Expired reset.
17. Session restore.
18. Refresh-token rotation.
19. Logout.
20. Password change invalidation.
21. RLS cross-user block.
22. Client role escalation rejected.
23. Password absent from logs.
24. Service-role absent from client bundle.
25. CloudFront current asset verification.
26. Registration health.
27. SMTP delivery.
28. Rate limiting.
29. Browser refresh/resume.
30. Step 4 context preservation.

Run:

- unit tests;
- integration tests;
- API contract tests;
- migration tests;
- frontend/browser tests;
- TypeScript;
- lint;
- production smoke tests.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — DEPLOYMENT AND ROLLBACK
==================================================

After all code-level critical tests pass:

1. Commit only related changes.
2. Execute database migration.
3. Deploy backend.
4. Deploy landing page.
5. Invalidate CloudFront.
6. Build APK only if shared mobile auth code changed.
7. Verify production health.
8. Run canary signup.
9. Run canary login.
10. Run recovery test.
11. Verify metrics.
12. Keep rollback commit and migration rollback ready.

Required owner approvals:

CONFIRM_IVX_GITHUB_WRITE
CONFIRM_IVX_RENDER_DEPLOY
CONFIRM_IVX_SUPABASE_MIGRATION
CONFIRM_IVX_CLOUDFRONT_INVALIDATION
CONFIRM_IVX_APK_UPLOAD only if APK changes

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

Do not mark complete until:

[ ] Production database constraints are active.
[ ] Custom SMTP is configured and tested.
[ ] CloudFront serves the current registration build.
[ ] New member signup succeeds from the live public landing page.
[ ] Exactly one Auth user is created.
[ ] Exactly one member/profile is created.
[ ] Exactly one investment-interest row is created.
[ ] Member can sign in.
[ ] Owner can sign in.
[ ] Invalid credentials are rejected.
[ ] Password reset works.
[ ] Session survives restart/refresh.
[ ] Logout/login works.
[ ] Non-owner cannot access owner routes.
[ ] Duplicate submission creates no duplicates.
[ ] Partial-account repair works.
[ ] RLS and role authorization pass.
[ ] Password and secrets never appear in logs.
[ ] Physical-device/browser tests are recorded honestly.
[ ] Metrics match actual records.
[ ] GitHub SHA matches runtime.
[ ] Live smoke tests pass after deployment.

FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

or

Do not return the general enterprise certification report.
This task is exclusively for completing registration and authentication end to end.
